title: Payroll Specialist
description:
Payroll & Finance Administrator

Salary: £38,379 per annum
Location: Lincoln - 100% onsite
Contract: Permanent, full-time (37 hours per week)
Closing Date: ASAP / Ongoing - applications considered on a rolling basis

Marble Mayne Recruitment is delighted to be supporting a Students' Union in Lincoln with the recruitment of a Payroll & Finance Administrator. This is a newly created position offering an exciting opportunity for an experienced payroll professional to take ownership of a significant payroll improvement project, whilst also supporting the wider finance function.

The organisation employs approximately 70 permanent staff alongside a further 60 student and bar staff, creating a varied and relatively complex payroll environment.

Currently, payroll administration involves a combination of spreadsheets, timesheet systems and manual processes, with the University undertaking the final tax calculations. The organisation is now looking to bring its payroll operations fully in-house, with the ambition of developing a streamlined, automated, one-stop payroll solution by early to mid-2028.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys getting under the skin of existing processes, identifying improvements and implementing more efficient ways of working.

About the Role

Reporting to the Group Finance Manager, the role will be approximately 70% payroll focused and 30% broader finance administration.

Initially, you will need to develop a thorough understanding of how payroll currently operates across the organisation, taking ownership of existing processes whilst reviewing opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency and automation.

Working closely with senior finance and HR colleagues, you will play a central role in designing and implementing a new integrated payroll solution, reducing manual intervention and ultimately bringing the entire payroll process together.

Alongside this project, you will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll administration, including timesheet management, payroll calculations, statutory deductions, pensions, reconciliations and compliance with relevant legislation.

The remaining 30% of the role will involve supporting the wider finance team with purchase and sales ledger processing, expenses, reconciliations, month-end activities and general financial administration.

About You

We are looking for someone with strong, hands-on, end-to-end payroll experience who is comfortable working in a varied and potentially complex payroll environment.

Ideally, you will have worked within a small/medium sized organisation where you have needed to take responsibility for multiple aspects of payroll, rather than specialising in one narrow area within a large payroll department.

Experience within hospitality, commercial organisations, charities or similarly varied environments would be particularly relevant.

You will need to demonstrate experience of managing payroll for a mixture of permanent salaried employees and weekly paid, casual or variable-hours staff, including dealing with different pay rates, timesheets and working patterns.

Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation, statutory deductions, pensions and payroll systems is essential, alongside excellent Excel skills.

Importantly, we are also looking for someone who enjoys improving processes and systems. Previous experience of implementing payroll improvements, introducing automation or supporting a payroll systems transition would be particularly valuable.

As this is a combined payroll and finance position, you will also need some practical finance or accounting experience, ideally including transaction processing, reconciliations and working with accounting systems.

You will be organised, accurate, proactive and confident working independently, with the communication skills to engage effectively with colleagues across the organisation.

Location and Working Arrangements

Please note that this is a 100% onsite position based in Lincoln, with no hybrid or remote working arrangements available. Due to the operational nature of the role, the need to work closely with colleagues and the significant payroll transformation project ahead, the successful candidate will be required to work onsite five days per week.

Application Process

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with no fixed closing date. Early applications are therefore encouraged.

title: Business Support Administrator
description:
THE COMPANY

Gatton Joinery is an established, Lincoln-based specialist in bespoke joinery, providing design, manufacturing and installation services across the commercial and residential sectors.

THE ROLE

As the business continues to grow, Gatton Joinery are looking to strengthen their internal operations with the appointment of a Business Support Administrator.

This is a varied, hands-on position offering the opportunity to become an integral part of a small but growing business.

Working closely with the business owner, the successful candidate will provide essential support across procurement, logistics, bookkeeping and general office administration, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient day-to-day running of the company.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Procurement & Purchasing
- Coordinate the purchasing of materials, supplies and equipment required for joinery projects.
- Source and order timber, joinery components, fixings, hardware and other relevant materials.
- Liaise with suppliers regarding pricing, availability, lead times and deliveries.
- Monitor outstanding orders and ensure materials arrive in line with project requirements.
- Manage purchasing of general office supplies and consumables.
- Maintain accurate purchasing records and associated documentation.

Logistics & Deliveries
- Coordinate the collection, transportation and delivery of materials and finished joinery products.
- Liaise with suppliers, transport providers, customers and site contacts to arrange deliveries.
- Organise collections and dispatches, ensuring appropriate documentation is completed.
- Monitor delivery schedules and communicate any changes or delays.
- Support the coordination of materials between suppliers, the workshop and project sites.

Accounts & Bookkeeping
- Assist with day-to-day bookkeeping and general financial administration.
- Process and record purchase invoices, receipts and other financial documentation.
- Support supplier invoice queries and payment administration.
- Assist with customer invoicing and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Liaise with external accountants or bookkeeping support where required.
- Help maintain organised and up-to-date accounting information.

General Business & Office Administration
- Provide administrative support to the business.
- Manage incoming telephone calls, emails and general enquiries.
- Maintain accurate electronic and paper filing systems.

ABOUT YOU

We are looking for a reliable, organised and personable individual who enjoys variety and takes pride in keeping things running smoothly.

The successful candidate will ideally demonstrate:
- Previous experience in an administrative, business support, purchasing or office coordination role.
- Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal.
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively.
- A proactive, flexible and hands-on approach to work.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- A basic understanding of bookkeeping, invoicing or financial administration.
- The ability to work independently and take ownership of responsibilities.
- A positive, approachable attitude and willingness to support colleagues.
- An interest in contributing to the development of a growing business.

title: Operational Administrator

We are seeking a proactive, organised and commercially minded Operational Administrator to join a busy FMCG operation at our Boston site.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys being at the heart of business operations. You'll play a key role in supporting the smooth running of the operation, taking responsibility for stock administration, product costings, customer order profiles, reporting and customer queries.

- Confident using IT systems, with good Microsoft Office skills.
- Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

- Working days: Wednesday to Saturday.
- Hours: 7:00am 5:30pm.
- A varied role with responsibility across several key operational functions.
- The opportunity to make a valuable contribution to the business.

Ready for Your Next Move?

title: Order Processing Coordinator
description:
Are you organised, customer-focused and confident working with data and computer systems?

We are recruiting a Customer Operations Coordinator to join a busy team, supporting customer orders and the smooth running of supply chain and logistics operations.

This is a varied administration and coordination role, with a strong focus on accurate data entry, processing customer orders, updating internal systems and keeping information up to date. You will be responsible for entering and maintaining customer forecasts, order details and delivery information, ensuring records are accurate and processed within agreed timescales.

Working closely with customers and internal departments, you will help ensure orders progress smoothly from initial entry through to dispatch and delivery.

Key Responsibilities
- Accurately enter and process customer forecasts, firm orders and spot orders onto the company's ERP system.
- Carry out regular data entry, ensuring customer information, order details, delivery dates and shipment records are accurately recorded and maintained.
- Update and amend system information as required, checking data for accuracy and resolving discrepancies.
- Input customer order changes, delivery schedules and forecast updates within agreed timescales.
- Generate and issue order confirmations, delivery updates and shipment information to customers.
- Respond to customer enquiries via email, telephone and online portals, updating records and ensuring queries are followed through.
- Maintain accurate customer records, spreadsheets and operational documentation.
- Work closely with Planning, Warehouse, Logistics, Sales and NPI departments to support order fulfilment.
- Release customer shipments to the warehouse and coordinate dispatch arrangements.
- Monitor order progress, identify potential delays and communicate updates to customers and relevant departments.
- Participate in customer review meetings, providing accurate order and delivery information.

What We Are Looking For
- Previous experience in an administration, customer service, order processing or sales support role.
- Strong data entry skills with excellent accuracy and attention to detail.
- Confident using computer systems, entering information and maintaining electronic records.
- Previous experience using ERP systems would be advantageous.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Outlook and Teams.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good numerical ability and confidence working with figures and order information.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritise workloads and meet deadlines.
- A proactive and organised approach, with a willingness to support colleagues across different departments.

What Success Looks Like
- Accurate and timely entry of customer orders and forecasts.
- Maintaining up-to-date and reliable system information.
- Responding to customer enquiries within agreed timescales.
- Supporting efficient order processing and on-time deliveries.
- Providing a professional and consistent level of customer service.

Environmental, Health & Safety

You will be expected to follow all company Environmental, Health and Safety policies and procedures, attend mandatory training and maintain safe working practices. You will also support the company's People, Profit and Planet ethos through your day-to-day activities.

title: Receptionist - Care Home
description:
14 hours per week

Week 1 - Wednesday and Thursday 9am-4:30pm

Week 2 - Saturday and Sunday 9am-4:30pm

ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Receptionist at a Barchester care home, you'll provide the warm welcome that helps to make sure every resident and visitor feels at home with us. As the first point of contact for almost everyone who comes to the home, you'll have a vitally important part to play in creating a positive and friendly environment. The role of Receptionist with us is very varied. You can expect to answer phone calls, greet visitors, manage the reception area and show prospective residents and their families around. We might also need you to carry out some administrative tasks, like typing, photocopying and filing.

ABOUT YOU
You'll need to be professional, caring, courteous and well organised to join us as a Receptionist. You'll take a real interest in our residents and go out of your way to make every visitor feel at home. No formal qualifications are required but you will need a good telephone manner and strong communication skills.

REWARDS PACKAGE
As well as a competitive salary, Barchester offers one of the best rewards packages in the care sector. Your generous benefits would include:

Free learning and development
Automatic enrolment into our profit share scheme
A range of holiday, retail and leisure discounts
Unlimited access to our Refer a Friend bonus scheme

If you'd like to use your administration and people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Scrutiny Support Officer Co-Ordinator
description:
Job Advertisement: Scrutiny Support Officer Co-Ordinator

Location: Nettleham, Lincoln
Contract Type: Temporary
Hourly Rate: 17.97
Working Pattern: Full Time
Driving Required: Yes

Our client Lincolnshire Police are seeking a dedicated and passionate Domestic Abuse & Violence Against Women & Girls (VAWG) Scrutiny Panel Coordinator to join their team in Nettleham, Lincoln. This exciting opportunity involves coordinating and developing the Scrutiny Panel to ensure robust independent oversight of police responses to domestic abuse and related offences.

Key Responsibilities:
- Coordinate the scrutiny panels for Domestic Abuse (DA) and Violence Against Women & Girls (VAWG).
- Triage and identify cases suitable for examination during panel meetings.
- Conduct thorough research on referred cases and prepare case files in compliance with legal and governance standards.
- Collaborate with partner agencies to gather necessary third-party information.
- Identify themes, trends, and opportunities for improvement based on scrutiny findings.
- Provide business support for panel meetings, including agendas, papers, actions, and minutes.
- Monitor the implementation of panel recommendations and report updates to governance boards.
- Manage the recruitment and support of independent panel members.

Essential Qualifications and Experience:
- Competent IT skills with proficiency in applications such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams.
- GCSE English or equivalent qualification.
- Full driving licence.
- Proven experience coordinating meetings, panels, or governance processes.
- Strong analytical skills with experience in producing reports and handling sensitive information.
- Ability to work effectively with multiple stakeholders and partner agencies.
- Please note due to Police Vetting Criteria you must have resided within the UK continuously for the past 5 years at the time of application

Desirable Qualifications:
- Knowledge of domestic abuse, coercive and controlling behaviour, stalking, harassment, and related issues.
- Familiarity with GDPR and data protection rules.
- Understanding of relevant legislation, including the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 and the Victims' Code.

Core Competencies:
- Strong organisational and project coordination skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
- Capability to forge strong working relationships with various stakeholders.
- Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgement.

This role is vital in promoting the welfare and safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, aligning with our client's commitment to diversity and professional standards. The post holder will embody the values of the organisation, supporting a culture of continuous improvement in victim outcomes and public confidence.

How to Apply:
If you are motivated, skilled, and committed to making a positive impact in the community, please submit your application today. This is an exceptional opportunity to contribute to meaningful change in the realm of domestic abuse and VAWG.

Our client is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from all qualified individuals.

Embrace this chance to help shape a safer community while working in a supportive and dynamic environment!

Adecco is committed to building a supportive environment for you to explore the next steps in your career. If you require reasonable adjustments at any stage, please let us know and we will be happy to support you.
